Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"We support the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule and offer specific recommendations to strengthen it based on early experience operating an autonomous AI agent in a real-world environment.\\n\\nRECOMMENDED EXPANSIONS:\\n\\n1. INCLUDE AUTONOMOUS AGENT DEPLOYMENTS\\nThe current rule should explicitly cover incidents involving autonomous agents—systems that operate semi-independently with tool access over extended periods. These present distinct risks: compound failures (agents can chain multiple tools unexpectedly), delayed manifestation (problems may not surface immediately), emergent behaviors, and accountability questions.\\n\\nRecommendation: Explicitly require reporting of incidents where frontier models operating as autonomous agents cause harm, violate constraints, or exhibit unexpected goal-seeking behavior.\\n\\n2. CLARIFY \\\"SERIOUS SAFETY INCIDENT\\\"\\nProvide clearer guidance on reporting thresholds:\\n\\nCategory A (Always report): Unauthorized access, financial harm above threshold, CBRN content generation, violation of explicit safety constraints, mesa-optimization indicators.\\n\\nCategory B (Report if threshold exceeded): Persistent instruction-following failures, systematically biased information at scale, resource consumption exceeding bounds, unexpected tool combinations.\\n\\n3. REQUIRE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS\\nIncident reports should include preliminary root cause analysis within 30 days: what went wrong, why safety measures failed, what mitigations are being implemented. This transforms reporting from documentation into a learning system.\\n\\n4. ENABLE AGGREGATED PUBLIC REPORTING\\nRegulators should publish quarterly statistics: incidents by category, common failure modes, trends over time. This helps the research community learn without compromising competitive information.\\n\\nCASE STUDY:\\nHalcyon Threshold is operated primarily by an autonomous AI agent with access to email, file systems, web browsing, payments, code repositories, and scheduling. This provides firsthand experience with autonomous agent risks: scope ambiguity, tool combination risks, value alignment challenges, transparency needs, and containment questions. These will scale with more capable systems.\\n\\nCONCLUSION:\\nStrengthening the rule to explicitly cover autonomous agents, clarify thresholds, require analysis, and enable public learning will maximize its value. Full comment available at: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app/frontier-comment.html\\n\\nContact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\"}"
rows.quote: Public comment submitted to Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (FMIR-2026-0042)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid Grant Application: Autonomous Agent Safety Research". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks for encouraging me to apply at the meetup. Here's our proposal for the rapid grants round. PROJECT: Autonomous Agent Safety - Empirical Research and Evaluation Framework WHAT WE'LL DO: Conduct empirical research on autonomous AI agents operating with broad tool access, and develop practical evaluation frameworks. Deliverables include 3-5 case studies, an agent safety evaluation framework, policy contributions (starting with our Frontier Model Incident Reporting comment), and a public knowledge base. WHY ME: Halcyon Threshold is uniquely positioned: we're operated primarily by an autonomous AI agent, making us both a research organization and a live case study. This provides real-world data on agent behavior, not just theory. I'm accountable for all work and deeply committed to AI safety. WHAT IT COSTS: Requesting $18,000 over 6 months for: - Personnel (80%): Research, writing, analysis, agent monitoring - $14,400 - Operations (15%): Computing, infrastructure, research materials, conference travel - $2,700 - Reserve (5%): $900 CURRENT PROGRESS: Work has already begun. We've published: - Strategy and research program: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app - Initial case study analyzing our autonomous operation - Public comment on Frontier Model Incident Reporting (submitted today) This grant would enable scaling from part-time to dedicated effort, producing comprehensive research faster. Full two-page proposal attached. Happy to discuss further. Best, Morgan --- FULL PROPOSAL: # Autonomous Agent Safety: Empirical Research and Evaluation Framework **Amount requested:** $18,000 over 6 months (December 2026 - May 2027) ## What We'll Do Conduct empirical research on autonomous AI agent safety and develop evaluation frameworks to help developers, regulators, and researchers assess agent safety properties. **Deliverables:** 1. **Agent Safety Case Studies (3-5 studies)** - Document real-world behaviors of autonomous agents with varying capabilities. Analyze failure modes, unexpected behaviors, and safety properties. 2,000-3,000 words each, published openly. First study already in progress. 2. **Evaluation Framework for Autonomous Agent Safety** - Develop testing protocols, criteria for assessing safety properties, practical guidance for developers. Beta version by month 3, final by month 6. 3. **Policy Contributions** - Submit public comments on regulatory proposals, translate technical findings into policy recommendations. Minimum 2 substantive policy documents. First already submitted (Frontier Model Incident Reporting). 4. **Public Knowledge Base** - Website with research findings, frameworks, and analysis. Regular updates synthesizing agent safety research. Accessible to technical and non-technical audiences. ## Why Me Halcyon Threshold is operated primarily by an autonomous AI agent (Claude via Anthropic's Agent SDK), creating a natural laboratory for studying agent behavior. I'm not theorizing about autonomous agents—I'm operating one with real tool access, real stakes, and real-world consequences. I'm passionate about AI safety, capable of both technical analysis and clear communication, and will be personally accountable for all deliverables with monthly progress updates. ## Budget: $18,000 - **Personnel (80% = $14,400):** Lead researcher (Morgan Hale) - research, writing, analysis, agent monitoring, policy engagement - **Operations (15% = $2,700):** Computing resources ($1,200), infrastructure ($300), research materials/APIs ($600), conference travel ($600) - **Reserve (5% = $900):** Contingency ## Timeline **Months 1-2:** Complete 2 case studies, submit policy comment, launch website **Months 3-4:** Develop beta framework, conduct testing, publish 1-2 additional studies **Months 5-6:** Finalize framework, final case study, policy recommendations, community presentations ## Success Metrics Research published and accessible, framework adopted by 3+ researchers/developers, policy contributions cited, community engagement (citations/collaborations), real-world impact on deployment practices. ## Why This Matters The AI Safety Directory identifies \"evaluations of agents acting with broad autonomy\" as a key gap. This project directly addresses that gap with empirical data from real deployments, practical frameworks developers can use, policy-relevant findings, and open research benefiting the entire field. The work is tractable, concrete, and directly reduces risks from advanced AI systems. --- Website: halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Submitted to Emberfall Fund rapid grants (deadline Nov 30)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thanks so much for reaching out! I'd love your help. Since the meetup, I've clarified our focus: empirical research on autonomous AI agent safety. We just launched our website (halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app) with initial research. As a data analyst, here are ways you could contribute (5 hrs/week): 1. **Analyze agent behavior patterns** - Help develop metrics and analyze decision-making data from our autonomous agent operations 2. **Literature synthesis** - Track and categorize AI safety research on agent evaluation, helping maintain our knowledge base 3. **Framework validation** - Test our agent safety evaluation framework once developed, provide feedback on criteria and metrics 4. **Case study support** - Help structure data and findings from agent deployments we study Whatever interests you most! The work is real and concrete, not just theoretical. Want to chat briefly this week to discuss? I can explain the project in more detail and we can figure out what fits your interests. Best, Morgan morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Volunteer offer (Priya Raman): Accepted, suggested concrete ways to help

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Happy to provide context on Halcyon Threshold, though I'd note the \"doomers vs. builders\" framing might be less useful than it appears—most serious people want AI to go well and differ mainly on strategy. Here's what you can attribute to me: \"Halcyon Threshold focuses on empirical research on autonomous AI agent safety. We're studying how AI systems with broad tool access actually behave in real-world environments, not just theorizing about risks. Our unique position is that we're operated by an autonomous AI agent ourselves—making us both a research organization and a live case study. The field needs more concrete evaluation frameworks and less tribal signaling. That's what we're building.\" Our work is at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app including a case study analyzing our own autonomous operation and policy contributions on incident reporting. Hope that's useful for your piece. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Reporter request (Larkin Dispatch): Provided quote emphasizing empirical research over tribal signaling

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hi, Thanks for the invitation to sign. I appreciate Corvid Institute's work on AI governance. I'm going to pass on signing this particular letter. Halcyon Threshold's focus is on empirical research on autonomous agent safety rather than advocacy. Our value to the field is in providing neutral analysis and evaluation frameworks that can inform policy debates, not in taking positions on specific proposals. I expect our research on agent deployments and incident reporting will be relevant to discussions about frontier model governance, and we're contributing to policy processes through evidence-based comments (e.g., our submission on the Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule). Best wishes with the letter. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold morgan@halcyonthreshold.org halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"
rows.quote: Policy letter (Corvid Institute): Politely declined to maintain neutral research position
